newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-INDIAN SPIN TAKES ON SOUTH AFRICA PACE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIAN SPIN TAKES ON SOUTH AFRICA PACE.

text.p: It will be a case of Indian spin versus South African pace when the two sides meet on Wednesday in the first test of their three-match series.
Little is known for certain about the status of the pitch for a five-day match but it is expected to take some turn by the third day, which should assist India's highly successful spin attack.
The South Africans have decided to field four pace bowlers with debutant Lance Klusener joining Allan Donald, Fanie de Villiers and Brian McMillan.
The spinner's place in the side will be a toss up between 36-year old Pat Symcox and the unorthodox Paul Adams.
The Indians are playing three spinners, according to captain Sachin Tendulkar.
Leg spinner Narendar Hirwani is expected to be back in the fray in place of Ashish Kapoor, joining vice-captain Anil Kumble and left arm spinner Sunil Joshi.

Indian spinners have been very successful in home tests and South African coach Bob Woolmer played down his side's easy victories in the two warm-up matches, against domestic champions Karnataka and a Board President's XI.
"The opposition was so weak each time that we did not get a chance to allow our batsmen to play long enough innings," he said.
India's Tendulkar made light of the problems facing his team but said he would certainly miss batsman Saurav Ganguly, who is not playing due to injury.
"We are also still looking for a stable opening pair. But we have enough talent around to bolster the side's batting."
Both Tendulkar and South African captain Hansie Cronje expect the test to be an engrossing contest.
"A victory here would mean a lot to us and we have the bowlers to help us achieve that on this wicket," said Tendulkar.
"I think we have a good contest on our hands and we have the all round talent to maintain our record," said Cronje.
South Africa played three home tests against India in their last and only series in 1992-93. They won at Port Elizabeth and the other two were drawn.
